\paragraph{Run completion.}
All three runs are complete. The original sweep evaluated $102$ configurations at $10$M steps
with $256$ copies each. The first extension, on 2026-08-16--17, tested each arm's selected
configuration at $1000$M steps with $1{,}024$ copies. The second extension, on 2026-08-17--18,
tested all $66$ configurations of random network distillation and the oracle $1/\sqrt{n}$ bonus
at $1000$M steps with $128$ copies each.

\paragraph{Metrics.}
A configuration is one algorithm with a specified learning rate and intrinsic weight.
Rewards are recorded in windows of $200$ training iterations, equivalent to $256$ complete
$400$-step episodes per copy. These windows cover the episode phases evenly.
The tables report means and standard errors over completed copies; the column $N$ gives
that copy count.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
\item \textbf{Whole-run reward:} mean episode return over the entire run; used to rank configurations.
\item \textbf{Max reward:} highest window mean, computed by averaging copies first and then
  taking the maximum. Its standard error is measured at that window.
\item \textbf{Last-window reward:} mean episode return in the final recording window.
\item \textbf{Success rate:} fraction of copies that reached the goal at least once.
\item \textbf{Maze-cell coverage:} percentage of the $46$ open cells visited during training.
\item \textbf{Steps to goal:} not recorded.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Findings.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{F\arabic*},leftmargin=*,labelsep=0.6em]
\item \textbf{Distillation improves reward at the two larger learning rates.} Random network distillation
  improves reward over training without a bonus at $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-4}$. At $10^{-5}$,
  both have zero reward, although distillation achieves higher coverage.
\item \textbf{Oracle bonuses do not consistently outperform distillation.} At $10$M steps, the oracle $1/\sqrt{n}$ bonus has higher reward
  than distillation, but $1/n$ has lower reward. The winning oracle's coverage is not clearly
  different from distillation's.
\item \textbf{The slower-decaying oracle bonus performs better on both metrics.} At $10$M steps, $1/\sqrt{n}$ achieves both higher coverage and
  higher reward than $1/n$.
\item \textbf{Reward peaks at an intermediate intrinsic weight.} At learning rate $10^{-3}$, reward has an interior peak
  and declines at larger intrinsic weights. Very small weights yield almost no reward,
  rather than a clear increasing sequence.
\item \textbf{The best settings depend on the training budget.} The $10$M-step sweep selects
  learning rate $10^{-3}$; the $1000$M-step sweep selects $10^{-4}$ and an intrinsic weight
  ten times larger for both re-swept arms. At the long budget, these settings achieve about
  $29$ times the reward for distillation and $58$ times the reward for the oracle bonus
  compared with the settings selected at $10$M steps.
\item \textbf{Distillation has higher reward at the long budget.} With settings selected at
  $1000$M steps, its whole-run reward is $52.500 \pm 3.368$, compared with
  $38.199 \pm 3.216$ for the oracle $1/\sqrt{n}$ bonus. Both reach the goal in all $128$
  copies and achieve $99.85\%$ coverage.
\end{enumerate}

sec:pm-jax-corrected.text:
\label{sec:pm-jax-corrected}
At a 400-step reset, intrinsic advantages now continue into the next episode using the
intrinsic value of the reset observation. The immediate intrinsic bonus still scores the final
transition observation. Task-return bootstrapping and task advantage boundaries retain their
previous definitions. This matches CleanRL's continuing intrinsic-return convention.
For the no-bonus control, the intrinsic advantage now has weight zero, so its policy update
uses only task advantages. The shared two-head critic architecture is retained.

The 11 unique settings shown in Figures~\ref{fig:pm-jax-run11-curves} and
\ref{fig:pm-jax-run11-shapes} are retrained for 100M steps with 128 paired seeds per setting.
The learning rate is denoted by $\alpha$, and the weight on intrinsic advantage by $\beta$.
For the oracle bonuses, $n$ denotes the visit count of the discretized position and velocity state.
Only the listed pairs are trained; the experiment does not take their Cartesian product.

\paragraph{Findings.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{D\arabic*},leftmargin=*,labelsep=0.6em]
\item \textbf{The control reproduces the fall within $50$M steps.} At every weight the return peaks
  between $11$M and $29$M steps and the final tenth keeps $0.18$--$0.53$ of the peak.
\item \textbf{Annealing the learning rate within the run (A8) is the only idea that passes the test.}
  It keeps $0.98$--$0.99$ of its peak at every weight and ends at $64.9\pm4.3$ ($\beta=100$),
  twice the control's peak.
\item \textbf{Ending the episode at the goal (E1, E2) holds the peak but learns less.} Both keep
  $0.91$--$0.94$ of their peaks at the weights that learn, but end with $48$--$59\%$ of episodes
  reaching the goal, against $67.5\%$ at the control's peak. With a $-1$ step cost (E2) every
  weight learns; with $+1$ once (E1) the two largest weights do not.
\item \textbf{The entropy bonus (A4) gives the highest level but still falls.} Its peaks are near
  $90$, three times the control's, and its best final is $76.4$ ($\beta=1000$, $0.80$ of its peak).
  The log standard deviation it produces grows without limit (to $5$): clipped actions make a wide
  Gaussian cost nothing.
\item \textbf{The other algorithm ideas fall like the control.} Weight decay (A1), the goal-rate gate
  (A2), task-reward scaling (A5) and the discount $0.99$ (A6) keep $0.12$--$0.85$ of their peaks;
  clipping per network (A7) raises the peak to $43$ but keeps $0.14$--$0.59$ of it. Clipped PPO (A3)
  barely learns at learning rate $10^{-3}$ (best final return $0.49$): its sixteen clipped steps per
  rollout drive the log standard deviation to $-2.6$ within the first $2$M steps.
\item \textbf{The fall comes with a slowing ball, not with a shrinking action spread.} In every
  falling run the mean speed drops from about $5$ to $2$--$3$\,m/s
  (\Cref{fig:pm-jax-batch1-speed}); in the runs that hold (E1, E2, A8) it stays at $4$--$5$. The log
  standard deviation falls in both groups (\Cref{fig:pm-jax-batch1-logstd}). A reading consistent
  with this: in the original task the reward for staying inside the goal radius teaches the policy
  to brake, and the braking spreads to the rest of the maze, so the ball reaches the goal later.
  Ending the episode at the goal removes the reason to brake; a falling learning rate stops the
  drift.
\end{enumerate}

sec:pm-jax-decline-summary.text:
\label{sec:pm-jax-decline-summary}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{R\arabic*},leftmargin=*,labelsep=0.6em]
\item \textbf{What falls, and when.} The extrinsic return falls after its peak whenever the
  learning rate stays near its starting value long after the peak: within $50$M steps at
  $10^{-3}$, after about $170$M steps at $10^{-4}$. It falls with distillation and with the
  oracle count bonus, and on the medium maze also without any bonus
  (\Cref{sec:pm-jax-screening}).
\item \textbf{What comes with it.} In every falling run the ball slows, from about $5$ to
  $2$--$3$\,m/s, so it reaches the goal later; the action spread shrinks in falling and holding
  runs alike, and raising it with a floor does not stop the fall
  (\Cref{sec:pm-jax-decline-batch1,sec:pm-jax-decline-batch2}).
\item \textbf{What fixes it.} Annealing the learning rate to zero over the training budget, with
  an entropy coefficient of $0.01$ (C2), held at every setting of the confirmation except the two
  smallest distillation weights and the smallest oracle weight at $10^{-3}$, where the dip
  recovered to $0.81$--$0.85$ of the peak; it also reached the highest returns throughout
  ($92$--$106$ against the controls' peaks of $30$--$95$). The anneal alone (A8) held wherever the
  peak came late in the run, but at $10^{-4}$ it ended below the control's peak. Ending the episode at the goal with a $-1$ step cost and clipping the
  networks' gradients separately (B5) held at $10^{-4}$ and over $50$M steps at $10^{-3}$, but not
  over $100$M at $10^{-3}$, and it changes the task.
\item \textbf{What does not.} Floors on the log standard deviation, a shorter critic step, the
  extrinsic discount $0.99$, scaling the task reward, decaying or gating the intrinsic weight,
  clipped PPO at $10^{-3}$, and whitening the agent's input
  (\Cref{tab:pm-jax-batch1-holds,tab:pm-jax-batch2-holds,tab:pm-jax-batch3-holds}).
\item \textbf{Recommended setting} for the platform's distillation runs: learning rate annealed
  linearly to zero over the run's own budget, entropy coefficient $0.01$. Both are existing
  options of the training command: \texttt{-{}-ent-coef 0.01}, with \texttt{-{}-lr-anneal-iterations}
  left unset so the rate anneals over the run's own length; the trainer's defaults are unchanged.
\end{enumerate}
